column1: # Words, old > new, by check rewrite 18: site/reference/cli.md 2818 > 2943.

column6: note
Split in three sentences: what diagnose makes, what replay checks, the two links

The term Tool merged with the section's opening, after the sample: the sqlsource command of the SqlSource.Tool package, which asks your database about your queries and writes the sidecars; merges/MP-10.md. `sqlsource`, `SqlSource.Tool` 2 > 1 and `describe` 3 > 2: said in both texts, kept once

Merged into the term's definition and three bullets: describe connects and asks the parameters and columns of each query; you commit the sidecars, so a build needs no database; the build runs describe itself on a machine with a connection. Adds the command to a project: kept as the command of the package, where it is installed is #install-the-tool. `billing` 0 > 1: a new sentence says what the sample shows
The sample, byte for byte, moved up to open the section (rewrite guide 4)

Cut to one sentence: the tool describes the queries whose output is repository, methods or models, and the build checks each against its sidecar; it links describing.md#which-queries too. The owner holds each fact: the constant or token method of sql and models, the default repository, SQLSRC241 and SQLSRC244 for no current entry. `sql` 2 > 0 and `models` 2 > 1: the sentence on sql or models is the owner's; its last sentence, A project whose queries all have the output sql needs no tool, stands whole as a bullet of #install-the-tool (MP-11)

Cut to one sentence that keeps both links: from the sidecars the generator builds the models of these queries and the method of a repository or methods query; the owner's last paragraph holds both facts
A local tool of your repository, run in the folder at its root; merged with README.md:19's Once; merges/MP-11.md

Two bullets: the first command creates the manifest dotnet-tools.json, which records the tool and its version, commit it; a clone and a build server get the same version with dotnet tool restore, and a build that runs the tool starts it. To run the tool give it a connection: the closing paragraph. `dotnet-tools.json` 2 > 1: README.md:27 said it again

Two bullets: keep the tool at the package's version, the two released together under one version number (docs/publishing.md), update with dotnet tool update SqlSource.Tool; different versions can stop the tool reading the project, SQLSRC206. What else it needs: the closing paragraph. `SqlSource` 2 > 1: README.md:27 said it again
Once, at the root of the repository: the sentence under the sample; skip the first command if the repository has a tool manifest: its own sentence
The README's copy of the two install commands goes, the one fenced block that the phase removes: the same block, byte for byte, opens the section

Adds the sqlsource command, which describes your queries: the closing paragraph; step 5 (numeral 5 1 > 0) becomes the step that describes your first query, its link to start/first-query.md#describe kept. Commit the manifest and keep the version: said twice, kept in the bullets (`SqlSource.Tool` 1 > 0, `dotnet new tool-manifest` 1 > 0 is the first command). Old: 'A project that only keeps its SQL out of code files does not need it.' New: the bullet A project whose queries all have the output sql needs no tool (`sql` 0 > 1), and 'That is a project that uses SqlSource only to keep its SQL out of its code files.' Same rule
Five sentences: --help of the tool, --help after a command, --version; the arguments and the first table are describe's, and where diagnose and replay are

Two bullets: what the project or solution is, and that the folder alone is searched, with SQLSRC201 and SQLSRC202 each in its own sentence. Old: 'Only one may be given.' New: 'You can give only one.' Same rule
Two bullets: the C# projects that use SqlSource, the others left out and nothing said; every C# project must be restored, one with no queries too, SQLSRC220
Two bullets: a .sql path restricts the run, several can be given; each must be a file that a type of the run claims, SQLSRC212, and the run goes on. `.sql` 6 > 7: named once more in the second bullet
A bullet of the list above it
Two sentences, the condition first
Three bullets, one rule each

An opening paragraph and three bullets; the three places a connection came from are a vertical list. `--verbose` 4 > 7: the lead-ins name the option where the old text said it. Old: 'A database's line names where its connection came from, and never the connection: ...' New: 'The line of a database names where its connection came from, and never the connection.' and the list. Same rule

Two paragraphs. Old: '... never attach it to an issue, and send it privately when a maintainer asks for it.' New: 'Never attach a log to an issue.  Send it privately, when a maintainer asks for it.' Same rule

Two bullets: each run overwrites the file, so the five endings are refused, SQLSRC218; a --log path with = or ; is refused, SQLSOURCE_LOG's is not. Old: '... so that a slip on the command line never empties a file of your project (SQLSRC218).' New: 'Then a slip on the command line never empties a file of your project.' Old: 'It refuses a --log path that holds = or ; too, ...; a path from SQLSOURCE_LOG is not held to that.' New: 'The tool also refuses a --log path that holds = or ;.' and 'A path from SQLSOURCE_LOG is not held to that rule.' Same rules. `=` and `;` 5 > 6: the old it named them once less
Two sentences

The four runs that do not print the line are a vertical list. Old: 'A --check whose only errors are sidecars out of date does not print it, nor does a --watch, nor diagnose or replay, nor the run of a build, ...' New: 'These runs do not print the line:' and the list. Same rule

The paragraph becomes three lists: what is written *** wherever found whole (each --connection value; each connection value the driver repeats, as written, trimmed or as the driver writes it again); what else is written ***; what can appear as written (a value with neither = nor ; where a path goes or after --log or --env-file, a password shorter than four characters, a password that is the name of its logical database or dialect). Whole, at least four, shorter than four and alone are kept; checked with Redaction.cs and ConnectionSecret.cs. `***` 4 > 2: one stands over each of the first two lists
Two sentences in the bullet
The bullet keeps its first sentence; the log that cannot be finished, SQLSRC218, exit code 1 and the last line, is a paragraph under the list, the tool named as the one that reports
The lead-in holds the rule; It is the tool
Three sentences, SQLSRC220 with its condition
The rule in the lead-in, and the version in a sentence that states none and keeps both links to databases/index.md#supported-versions
Under the sample, which now opens the section, byte for byte; it introduces the list of what the words of the line mean

Three paragraphs and two bullets: the counts of --check; a name of --database that no query has gets a line of zeros; the name when close, the position otherwise; a solution with no project that uses SqlSource

In the three parts of a limit. Old: '- A project path or a .sql path through a symbolic link is not found. When the current folder is reached through a symbolic link and ...' New: What you see: 'A project path or a .sql path through a symbolic link is not found, though the file is there.' Why: the current folder reached through the link, the full path through it, compared with the real path. Same rule
